A few words about my path

From Chios, to the courts, to psychotherapy

  1. 1963 · Chios

    The roots

    I was born in Chios in 1963 and lived there until I was ten. I have lived in Athens ever since.

    My first degree is from the University of Athens, in the Department of Political Science and Public Administration (NKUA).

  2. until 2014

    At the courts of Athens

    My working life began as a court clerk at courts in Athens, where I worked until 2014.

    From early on I was drawn to observing the human psyche and how people express themselves — and how this is shaped by their surroundings — an interest that grew through what I took in from my work.

  3. The training

    Body-Reichian psychotherapy

    At a more mature stage, alongside my job, this interest led me to train in counselling and psychotherapy — and, in time, to work professionally in what I truly loved.

    I chose to train in body-Reichian psychotherapy and counselling at the Hellenic Institute of Vegetotherapy and Character Analysis – Wilhelm Reich Centre, a training centre that since 1979 has followed and developed in Greece the revolutionary theory and therapeutic approach founded by Wilhelm Reich some 90 years ago.

  4. 2 years of practice

    «18 ANO» & a parents’ group

    After graduating I completed two years of practice in a residential addiction programme at «18 ANO», under supervision. At the same time, for two years, I facilitated a parents’ group at the Wilhelm Reich Centre for Counselling and Psychotherapy.

    Alongside my core training and practice — and to this day — I attend trainings and seminars, because I believe that continuing education, personal growth and, of course, supervision are essential in every mental health profession.

  5. since 2016

    Private practice

    Since 2016 I have offered in-person and online psychotherapy and counselling sessions to adults, couples, parents and groups, under ongoing supervision.

  6. 2024 – 2026

    Collective action

    My interest in the social dimension of counselling and psychotherapy, and my belief in collective action, lead me to take an active part in scientific and professional bodies in my field.

    I am a member of the Panhellenic Association of Body Psychotherapy (P.E.SO.PS) and of the Hellenic Association for Counselling, where I served as an elected board member for 2024–2026 while taking part in its committees, of which I remain a member.

    I have spoken at events of social and scientific organisations, and I regularly take part in Greek and international mental health conferences and meetings.

  7. 2026 – 2027

    Trainer

    From the 2026–2027 academic year I am a trainer in the counselling programme of the «The Art of Living» (Η Τέχνη του Ζην) centre.

Through my personal and professional journey I have come to believe deeply in the words of the French writer André Breton:

“Man is the answer, whatever the question.”

— André Breton

The human being who has the responsibility and the freedom to live their life consciously on every level — a stance that is not a given. It is an inner choice and an evolving path, and I am convinced that psychotherapy and counselling work as both a motivation and a support along it.

The therapeutic approach

Mind and body, one experience

Psychotherapy is a process of self-knowledge and connection with the authentic self, a support in facing difficulties and a path of self-realisation.

In my therapeutic work, what matters to me is creating a safe space where a person can trust and connect.

Contact with oneself on a bodily, emotional and mental level

Psychotherapy

The body-oriented (Reichian) approach

The body-oriented approach in which I have trained and practise is a psychodynamic approach that brings bodily experience into the diagnostic and therapeutic process. It allows a deeper exploration of unconscious experiences and processes, and the recognition and working-through of the patterns that shape the way we exist.

Through connection with bodily and emotional memory and experience, parts of our personal story emerge that are not always easy to reach through words alone.

In a setting of safety and acceptance, a deeper understanding of and contact with oneself becomes possible — on a bodily, emotional and mental level. Awareness widens across every level of experience, inner freedom grows, and new ways of being and relating authentically develop.

Counselling

Body-oriented counselling

Through counselling, people can get help with specific difficulties they face in the present, find support and make decisions about their lives.

Body-oriented counselling has the tools to bring relief and to empower a person who chooses a shorter process, focused on the issues that concern them.

One breath

Space and time to breathe

The body is where the work begins. Before anything else, take three slow breaths here with the seed of life — breathe in as it opens, breathe out as it closes.

Inhale 4 seconds · hold 2 · exhale 6

Breathe

A journey of connection, self-discovery and self-realisation.

Sessions offered

For you, your couple, your family, a group

In person at the practice in Ampelokipi or online, always under ongoing supervision.

Individual counselling & psychotherapy

More and more, in a chaotic and disconnected social reality, people need space and time to “breathe” and to connect with their own personal meaning. Psychotherapy and counselling are a journey of connection, self-discovery and self-realisation.

Couples counselling

For couples who find it hard to communicate or to live together with equality and closeness, and who want to support and improve their relationship — and for couples who struggle to make decisions about where their relationship is going.

Parent counselling

Support for today’s family, where parents face constant challenges in their role. Through counselling, a parent works with their anxiety, learns experientially about their role and strengthens their sense of personal power, so they can meet the responsibility of parenthood in a positive and effective way.

Adult therapy group

A process that helps people see clearly the difficulties in how they treat themselves and their relationships, recognise their needs and feel that their problems are not theirs alone but shared by most people. The mirroring and support a person receives in a therapy group is a valuable experience that develops their perception and their inner strength.

Where is the practice?

At 16-18 Eslin Street in Ampelokipi, Athens (postcode 115 23), a 5-minute walk from Ampelokipi metro station (line 3).

Do you offer online sessions?

Yes. Since 2016 I have offered both in-person and online psychotherapy and counselling sessions, so the work can continue even when travelling is not easy.

What is body psychotherapy?

It is a psychodynamic approach that brings bodily experience into the therapeutic process. Through connection with bodily and emotional memory, parts of our personal story emerge that are hard to reach through words alone.

What is the difference between psychotherapy and counselling?

Counselling is a shorter process, focused on specific present difficulties and life decisions. Psychotherapy is a deeper process of self-knowledge that explores the patterns shaping the way we exist.

Who are the sessions for?

Adults, couples, parents and adult therapy groups.

How does a therapy group help?

In a group, each person sees their difficulties with themselves and in relationships more clearly and feels that their problems are shared by most people. The mirroring and support of the other members is a valuable experience.

Is your work supervised?

Yes. All sessions take place under ongoing supervision, and I keep training, because supervision and continuing education are essential in every mental health profession.

How do I book a session?

Sessions are by appointment. Call 694 777 5084 or email theotokamaria@gmail.com and we will find a day and time together.
